title: The Unreliable Storyteller
text:
An unreliable narrator is a storyteller whose account cannot be fully trusted by the reader. Such narrators may lie, forget important details, or misunderstand what they witness. Readers must therefore compare the narrator's words with other clues in the text to reach their own conclusions.

This technique became popular in the twentieth century, when novelists wanted to explore the gap between what people say and what they believe. Some critics find it frustrating, yet many readers enjoy the challenge of uncovering the truth themselves.

questions.text: What can an unreliable narrator do, according to the first paragraph?
According to the second paragraph, what did novelists want to explore?
options: The gap between what people say and believe

questions.text: Why might readers need to compare the narrator's words with other clues?
options: Because the narrator's account may not be reliable
Because the book has no ending
Because clues are always printed in bold
Because the publisher asks them to

questions.text: What does the author suggest about readers who enjoy this technique?
options: They find satisfaction in working out the truth

vocabulary.definition: not able to be trusted or depended on
the person who tells a story
causing annoyance or a sense of being blocked
something difficult that tests one's skill

paragraph_translations: Um narrador não confiável é um contador de histórias cujo relato não pode ser totalmente confiável para o leitor. Esses narradores podem mentir, esquecer detalhes importantes ou entender mal o que presenciam. Por isso, os leitores precisam comparar as palavras do narrador com outras pistas do texto para chegar às próprias conclusões.

Essa técnica se tornou popular no século XX, quando romancistas quiseram explorar a distância entre o que as pessoas dizem e o que acreditam. Alguns críticos a consideram frustrante, mas muitos leitores gostam do desafio de descobrir a verdade por conta própria.
